chunk_findings.detail: `uncommitted_shards` parses `git status --porcelain` by slicing `line[3:]` and keeping entries whose stripped form `endswith(".jsonl")`. Porcelain v1 C-quotes any path that contains a space or a byte >= 0x80 (`core.quotePath` defaults to true), e.g. a shard created from an item name the user supplied with a space or non-ASCII text is reported as `?? ".ddflow/events/Monster3-my item-1.jsonl"` or `?? ".ddflow/events/Monster3-caf\303\251-1.jsonl"`. After `line[3:].strip()` the string ends with `"`, not `.jsonl`, so the `endswith` filter silently drops it. Since the shard name embeds the item (`Monster3-<item>-…`), and items come from the CLI, this is reachable. Consequence: the entry is never added to `shards`; if it is the only uncommitted shard, `commit_shards` returns `("", "")` — the documented "nothing to commit" success value — with no error text, so the caller reports success and the shard stays uncommitted forever, i.e. the exact failure Bcd3512c891 is supposed to fix, and `ddflow doctor` (which also uses this function per the config doc) will not list it either. Note that de-quoting is not enough on its own: even if the filter matched, the quoted string would be handed to `git add`/`git commit` as a literal pathspec and fail with "pathspec … did not match any files"; the output needs `-z` (or `-c core.quotePath=false` plus unquoting) to be parsed correctly.

chunk_findings.detail: The guard resolves `.ddflow/events` against the working tree of whatever checkout `git push` is issued from. Per the bug statement the shards for worktree agents live in the **primary** checkout's `.ddflow/events`, not in the linked worktree's tree. Concretely: an agent whose identity is `Monster3-<item>` works in a linked worktree `W` and runs `git push` from `W`. Git runs the hook with cwd = `W`, so line 39 executes `git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all -- .ddflow/events` inside `W`; that pathspec names `<W>/.ddflow/events`, which does not contain the shard that was written to `<primary>/.ddflow/events`. `git status` therefore prints nothing, `grep -c` yields `0`, and no warning is emitted — the very push that "publishes an incomplete history" (the scenario Bcd3512c891 is about) goes out silently. chunk_findings.detail:
`uncommitted_shards` parses non-`-z` `git status --porcelain` output by taking `line[3:].strip()` and keeping it only if it `.endswith(".jsonl")`. Non-`-z` porcelain C-quotes any path containing a byte outside `0x20..0x7e` (and `"`/`\`/control chars), because `core.quotePath` defaults to true; the quoted form is wrapped in double quotes with octal escapes, so it ends in `"`, not `.jsonl`. Concretely: with an event shard `.ddflow/events/Monster3-café-<item>.jsonl` untracked in the primary, git prints `?? ".ddflow/events/Monster3-caf\303\251-<item>.jsonl"`; line 29's filter rejects that line, so the shard is dropped from the returned list. If it is the only shard, `commit_shards` returns `("", "")` and the caller reports "nothing to commit" — the shard stays untracked and a clone/pull again gets an incomplete log, silently, which is exactly the bug Bcd3512c891 this change exists to fix (the failure is environment-dependent: with `core.quotePath=false` the same shard parses and is committed). The same parse is also wrong for rename entries (`R  old.jsonl -> new.jsonl`), where `line[3:]` yields `old.jsonl -> new.jsonl` and is passed as a single pathspec to `git add`, which fails; that path at least surfaces an error rather than dropping the shard. Using `git status --porcelain -z` (and splitting on NUL) or `-c core.quotePath=false` removes both failure modes.

Regarding the rest of the visible code: the pathspec-scoped `git add`/`git commit` pair correctly leaves other staged work untouched, the `_busy` guard runs before `add`, and the concurrent-interleaving case (two agents committing the same shards) degrades to a non-fatal "nothing to commit" for the loser, so I have nothing further to report there.

chunk_findings.detail: The new check inspects whatever working tree the hook happens to run in. Per the intent, shards are written into the **primary** checkout's `.ddflow/events`, while agents work and run git (and push) from linked worktrees. In a linked worktree, `git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all -- .ddflow/events` reports only that worktree's tree/index; untracked shards sitting in the primary are invisible to it. Concrete failure: primary checkout has 32 untracked `.ddflow/events/Monster3-T1-….jsonl` files; `git worktree add ../wt some-branch && cd ../wt && git push origin some-branch` → `loose` is `0`, no warning is printed, and the push silently publishes the incomplete log the warning was added to flag. chunk_findings.detail: The detection was changed to inspect the *primary* checkout (`git -C "$primary" status ...`), but the remediation message printed on the next lines is unchanged and is meant to be run in the current checkout. Concrete failure: an agent inside a linked worktree runs `git push`; the primary has one uncommitted shard, so `loose` is 1 and the warning fires. The user runs the printed `git add .ddflow/events && git commit -m 'events' -- .ddflow/events` from the worktree; that stages/commits the *worktree's* `.ddflow/events` (which does not contain the shard), so the primary shard stays uncommitted, the push still publishes an incomplete log, and the very next push warns again. Before this change the warning only ever fired for shards in the current checkout, so the advice was actionable; now it points at the wrong working tree in exactly the worktree case the change was written for. The message should tell the user to run the command under `$primary` (or prefix it with `git -C "$primary"`).

chunk_findings.detail: `--path-format` for `rev-parse` only exists in git ≥ 2.31, and this is a client-side hook that runs on contributors' machines, not a pinned CI runner. On an older git, `git rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-common-dir` exits non-zero and prints an error (no `2>/dev/null`, no `|| ...`), the command substitution yields an empty string, `dirname ""` yields `.`, and the subsequent check runs `git -C "." status ...` in the pushing worktree. A contributor with git 2.30 pushing from a linked worktree therefore sees a spurious git error on every push and the check silently inspects the linked worktree instead of the primary, so the uncommitted shards in the primary are never counted and no warning is emitted. The same silent false negative occurs whenever the inner `rev-parse` fails for any reason.
